subject: Commit-swap proposal: shadow DR pools, cross-region routing fees & throughput SKUs
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Rios <diego@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-29T10:14:00-04:00
Subject: Commit-swap idea for multi-region Dedicated (short note)

Diego — great speaking this morning. Per our conversation, I wanted to put a short proposal on the table that addresses two things Acme asked for: predictable throughput in primary region (us-east) and a low-friction DR posture in eu-west without paying full double capacity.

High-level idea: allow a monthly "commit-swap" buffer where up to 25% of committed GPU capacity can be designated as a shadow/DR pool in a second region. The pool would be kept warm (minimal VM instances running for KV cache/fast startup) and billed at a reduced standby rate, with credits applied if you never fail over. On failover we convert shadow capacity to active at full throughput pricing.

Pros: keeps your primary SLOs intact, lowers the capital hit for geo-redundancy, and gives us a runway for routing tests. Open questions for procurement: how to reflect credits/proration when the swap is used, minimum term for swapped capacity, and exact standby rate.

I attached a short term-sheet draft and a SKU throughput breakdown from the product team. Priya — looping you for throughput SLO numbers and onboarding notes.

Next step: Diego, if you like the concept I can ask Logan on pricing side for a credit framework and produce a redlineable term sheet.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

From: Diego Rios <diego@acme-analytics.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Analytics Procurement <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T09:02:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Commit-swap idea for multi-region Dedicated (short note)

Marcus — thanks, conceptually this is exactly what we were hoping to see. A few clarifying points from our side before procurement engages formally:

- Can standby credits be accrued and redeemed month-to-month (we want to avoid a long backlog of credits that require settlement at renewal)?
- If we do periodic failover tests (we run a 2-hour DR failover drill monthly), does that count as a full conversion to active for billing?
- Are there any cross-region network egress fees or additional routing surcharges when we send inference traffic between us-east and eu-west?

Procurement — please advise what documentation you need to start a commercial review.

Diego Rios
Head of Platform, Acme Analytics
diego@acme-analytics.com

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Rios <diego@acme-analytics.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-10-01T11:20:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Commit-swap idea for multi-region Dedicated (throughput and failover notes)

Diego / Marcus — quick technical notes to make sure SLOs are realistic:

- Throughput SKU: our 4xA100 reserved GPU SKU gives 30k tokens/s sustained per pool for 512-token avg inference. If you keep 25% as shadow, that maps to ~7.5k tokens/s standby capacity.
- Warm standby behavior: we keep model weights loaded and KV caches primed to the last checkpoint. This means cold-starts are <300ms for the first few requests; p99 steady-state during conversion is typically in the 120–220ms range depending on sequence length.
- DR test policy: short scheduled failover drills (<=2 hours) will be treated as "exercise" and billed at the reduced standby rate unless you declare them a production failover. We will log and timestamp drills and share usage reports to avoid billing surprises.
- Routing costs: there is a modest cross-region routing surcharge when we proxy live requests across regions (network egress + orchestration overhead). Typical surcharge is $0.015 per 1k tokens in our current pricing model but can be rolled into committed discounts for large multi-region commits.

I've dropped the throughput SKU breakdown in the attached xlsx. Marcus — happy to run a short perf test with Acme's dev team next week.

—Priya
Priya Natarajan
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.ai

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Rios <diego@acme-analytics.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Acme Analytics Procurement <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T08:37:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Commit-swap idea for multi-region Dedicated (pricing/credits framework)

Diego / team — copying in pricing. We can make the swap work commercially with a few guardrails. Proposed pricing framework (high level):

1) Standby rate = 30% of active committed rate (applies to designated shadow capacity). Standby billed monthly.
2) Credit accrual: if shadow capacity is never converted during a billing month, 50% of the monthly standby fee is credited as an off-invoice credit that can be applied to future months within the same 12-month commitment period. Credits do not carry past the commitment term.
3) Failover conversion: on a customer-declared production failover, shadow capacity converts to active and is billed at the full active rate from the timestamp of conversion; standby credits for that month are voided for the converted capacity.
4) DR exercise exceptions: up to 4 scheduled drills per year (each <=2 hours) will not trigger conversion billing. Unscheduled failovers count as production failover.
5) Cross-region routing surcharge: reduce to $0.01 per 1k tokens for deals > 100M tokens/mo or fold into a flat bundled SKU for large commits.

If Acme is happy with these guardrails, we can produce a redlineable term sheet and SOW. To be explicit on discounts: multi-region bundle discount tiers start at 10% for 12-month commits and increase to 18% for 24-month commits; the swap standby rate above is additive to that.

Procurement note: we can add a “swap schedule” appendix to the MSA that enumerates which pool sizes are shadowed per month and the mechanics for conversion (API signal + signed PO trigger).

Logan Wright
Director, Pricing & Packaging, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.ai

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Rios <diego@acme-analytics.com>, Acme Analytics Procurement <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-02T16:45:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Commit-swap proposal: next steps and SOW request

Diego / procurement — thanks for the quick turn. Sounds like we have a path forward. Action items: 

1) Diego / procurement: confirm whether monthly credit accrual is acceptable (Logan's framework suggests 50% off-invoice credit that must be consumed within term).
2) Acme to confirm desired standby % (we proposed 25% but can set per-pool).
3) Redwood (Priya + Marcus): schedule a 45-minute perf & failover runbook review with your platform team next week (Priya to coordinate).
4) Redwood legal/commercial: we'll send an initial SOW and the swap appendix to the MSA. Attached is a draft SOW (SOW_Acme_v3.docx) and the term-sheet.

Diego — if you sign off on the credit approach + standby %, I'll circulate a DocuSign for the term-sheet and route the SOW to your procurement inbox.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
